title: sim-run guard and older sim-run edges: the watchdog stops under stty tostop; a KILL fallback can orphan a hung list group; a group kill aimed at sim-run misses the watchdog; a TERM before the shim starts prints perl source; die appends the exit code to its message; a TERM during a hung pre-check is held until the lists end
evidence: Review of PR 1435 (R9-R11, low): with stty tostop the watchdog, now its own process group, gets SIGTTOU on its first stderr write and stops (fix: trap TTOU in watch_devices, now ios/scripts/sim-guard.sh:58; end_watch at :82); end_watch KILL leaves a hung list in its own group (only after an external SIGSTOP); after a SIGKILL of sim-run the watchdog lives up to ~45 s holding stderr. Older, already on main: on_signal (sim-run.sh:407) runs `wait` on the SHIM perl source when TERM/INT lands before the shim starts (about 30 lines printed); `die` (sim-run.sh:51) prints $* including the code ("... 75"); a TERM during a hung pre-check waits up to ~30 s
